original_paper.title: A Nonparametric Sum of Ranks Procedure for Relative Spread in Unpaired Samples
original_paper.authors: Sidney Siegel and John W. Tukey
original_paper.journal: Journal of the American Statistical Association
original_paper.access_boundary: Publisher metadata and abstract were read. The publisher body was access-controlled, so no complete original-paper body read, hidden derivation, table value, or paper-file hash is claimed.

official_method_record.organization: National Institute of Standards and Technology
official_method_record.title: Siegel Tukey Test
official_method_record.normalization_note: Scripts and styles removed, HTML tags stripped, entities decoded, and whitespace collapsed. Raw HTML carries a request-varying email-obfuscation token, so the stable normalized visible-text hash is the reproducible content binding.
verified_claims: combine the two samples and sort the pooled observations ascending
assign rank 1 to the smallest, rank 2 to the largest, rank 3 to the next largest, rank 4 to the second smallest, and continue the alternating-extremes pattern
apply a Mann-Whitney rank-sum test to those assigned ranks
the command supports lower-, upper-, and two-sided alternatives
the page identifies the test as a two-sample nonparametric equal-dispersion procedure
the documented small-sample example uses exact inference
adverse_findings: the method record concerns independent samples rather than overlapping WTI formation blocks
the test is sensitive to relative spread and can also be affected by location differences when samples are not aligned
the EA uses the arithmetic only as a deterministic tail-occupancy state and makes no inferential claim
the exact half-support gate is a QM activity choice, not a NIST critical value

carrier_record.role: broad own-return continuation family and explicit NYMEX WTI membership only

exact_support_check.calculation: complete deterministic enumeration of all C(16,8) label assignments

claim_boundary: The records support the named alternating-extremes rank construction, original peer-reviewed method lineage, broad own-return continuation family, and WTI carrier membership only. They do not test fixed eight-by-eight monthly-return blocks, the half-support activity gate, one-month continuation, CFDs, fixed risk, activity, profitability, or decorrelation. The EA imports no external source, executable code, optimizer, random output, or trained output.
